sections.generalInfoText: We process personal data only to the extent necessary to provide a functional website, respond to inquiries, present our services, and operate our business communication in a secure and efficient manner.
sections.generalInfoText2: Processing is carried out in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable German data protection laws.
sections.generalInfoText3: Personal data is not transferred to third parties unless this is necessary for the technical operation of the website, for the performance of a contract or pre-contractual measures, for compliance with a legal obligation, on the basis of your consent, or otherwise permitted by law.
sections.legalBasesIntro: Where we process personal data, we rely in particular on the following legal bases:
legalBasesList: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR: performance of a contract or pre-contractual measures
Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR: compliance with a legal obligation
sections.legalBasesNote: Where processing is based on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, our legitimate interests lie in the secure, stable, efficient, and user-oriented operation of our website, the professional presentation of our company, and our business communication.
sections.serverLogs: Website Access Data and Server Log Files
sections.serverLogsIntro: When you access our website, information is automatically collected by our hosting provider in so-called server log files. This may include:
serverLogsList: Access status and HTTP status code
sections.serverLogsNote: This data is processed to ensure the stability, security, and technical functionality of the website and to detect, prevent, and investigate misuse or security-related incidents.
sections.serverLogsRetention: Server log data is generally stored for a maximum of 7 days unless longer retention is required for the investigation of security-related incidents or to assert, exercise, or defend legal claims.
sections.contactForm: Contact by Email or Contact Form
sections.contactFormText: If you contact us by email or submit an inquiry via our contact form, we process the personal data you provide for the purpose of handling your inquiry and communicating with you.
sections.contactFormRequired: Mandatory fields in the contact form are marked accordingly. These data are required in order to process your request.
contactFormLegalList: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR, if your inquiry relates to pre-contractual measures or the performance of a contract
Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, for general business communication and other inquiries
sections.contactFormNote: Your data will not be shared with third parties unless this is necessary to process your request, required by law, or otherwise legally permitted.
sections.contactFormProcessor: For the technical receipt and processing of form inquiries we use the Supabase platform (Supabase Inc., USA) as a processor pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR. The database used for this purpose is hosted in the EU (data centre region Ireland). Where personal data is transferred to third countries in this context, the transfer is based on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses.
sections.contactFormEmail: To send the e-mails generated when you submit one of our forms (forwarding your inquiry to our team and an automatic confirmation of receipt to you), we use the service Resend, provided by Plus Five Five, Inc., 2261 Market Street #5039, San Francisco, CA 94114, USA, as a processor pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR. Your form data, in particular name, e-mail address, company and message, is transmitted to Resend and processed in the USA. Resend is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; the data processing agreement additionally includes the EU Standard Contractual Clauses. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (processing your inquiry) and Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (reliable delivery).
sections.contactFormRetention: We store your inquiry only for as long as necessary to process it. Where statutory retention obligations apply, storage may continue for the duration required by applicable law.
sections.abuseProtectionText: To protect our forms against spam and abuse, we store the IP address, the browser identifier (user agent), the e-mail address provided, the time, the form source, the result of the check and a checksum of the content in a log in our database (Supabase) when a form is submitted.
sections.abuseProtectionLegal: Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our legitimate interest lies in the security of our forms and the prevention of abuse.
sections.abuseProtectionRetention: Log entries are deleted automatically after 30 days.
sections.provisionOfDataText: The provision of personal data is neither legally nor contractually required. However, certain information may be necessary for us to process and respond to your inquiry. If you do not provide the relevant data, we may be unable to handle your request.
sections.hostingNote: Hetzner Online GmbH processes personal data on our behalf on the basis of a data processing agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR. Data processing takes place on servers located in Nuremberg, Germany.
sections.cookiesText: This website uses technically necessary cookies and similar storage technologies (such as localStorage) required for the secure and proper operation of the website.
sections.cookiesText2: No marketing, profiling or advertising tracking technologies are used. For anonymous audience measurement we use Plausible Analytics, which works without cookies and without storing anything on your device (see the section “Audience measurement with Plausible Analytics”).
sections.cookiesText3: Where optional external content is available, your preference may be stored locally on your device using browser storage. This is not used for tracking purposes.
sections.cookiesText4: You can view and change your choices at any time through the Privacy Settings link in the footer of this website.
sections.cookiesLegal: Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our legitimate interest lies in the secure and efficient provision of our website.
sections.analyticsText: We use the web analytics service Plausible Analytics, provided by Plausible Insights OÜ, Västriku tn 2, 50403 Tartu, Estonia, to understand how our website is used, for example which pages are viewed, which websites visitors come from, which device types and countries occur and how often contact, booking and download buttons are used.
sections.analyticsText2: Plausible does not set cookies and does not store any information on your device. Your IP address and browser identifier are not stored; they are only used briefly, together with a random value that changes daily, to create an anonymous identifier for counting visits. The random value is deleted after 24 hours. We cannot identify you personally. The data is processed on servers in Germany.
sections.analyticsLegal: Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our legitimate interest lies in the statistical analysis and improvement of our website. Plausible processes the data as a processor pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR. You may object to this processing at any time (Art. 21 GDPR).
sections.googleMapsText: This website offers the option to display an interactive map provided by Google Maps (Google Ireland Limited, Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland). Google Maps is loaded only after you have given explicit consent.
sections.googleMapsText2: When Google Maps is activated, your IP address and technical connection data may be transmitted to Google servers, which may be located outside the European Economic Area.
sections.googleMapsText3: Your consent preference is stored locally on your device using browser storage (localStorage). No data is transmitted to Google until you opt in.
sections.googleMapsText4: You can withdraw your consent at any time through the Privacy Settings link in the footer or directly on the contact page.
sections.googleMapsMoreInfo: For more information, see the Google Privacy Policy at https://policies.google.com/privacy.
sections.turnstileText: This website uses Cloudflare Turnstile (Cloudflare, Inc., 101 Townsend St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA) to protect contact forms from automated abuse and bot submissions.
sections.turnstileText2: As soon as you interact with one of our forms, for example by clicking into an input field, Cloudflare Turnstile is loaded. Cloudflare may then process technical data such as your IP address, browser type and interaction behavior to determine whether the submission comes from a human user. No connection to Cloudflare is made before this interaction.
sections.turnstileText3: Cloudflare processes this data as a processor on the basis of our instructions. The data is used exclusively for abuse prevention and is not used for tracking, profiling, or advertising purposes.
sections.turnstileLegal: Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our legitimate interest lies in protecting our contact forms from spam and automated abuse. Turnstile is used as a strictly necessary security measure within the meaning of Section 25(2) No. 2 TDDDG.
sections.turnstileMoreInfo: For more information, see the Cloudflare Privacy Policy at https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/.
sections.calendlyText: For online appointment scheduling we integrate the Calendly service provided by Calendly LLC, 271 17th St NW, Atlanta, Georgia 30363, USA. The booking calendar is only loaded after you have expressly consented in the booking dialog. No data is transferred to Calendly before you give consent.
sections.calendlyText2: Once the calendar is loaded, your IP address and technical connection data are transferred to Calendly. If you book an appointment, Calendly additionally processes the details you enter (e.g. name, email address, selected time slot, optional message). Processing also takes place on servers in the USA; the transfer is based on appropriate safeguards pursuant to Art. 44 et seq. GDPR (EU Standard Contractual Clauses or certification under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework).
sections.calendlyText3: You may withdraw your consent at any time with effect for the future – directly in the booking dialog via “Withdraw consent” or by clearing this website's local browser data.
sections.calendlyLegal: Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR (consent); for carrying out a booked appointment, Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR.
sections.calendlyMoreInfo: Further information is available in Calendly's privacy policy: https://calendly.com/privacy
sections.dataRetentionText: Personal data is stored only for as long as necessary for the respective processing purpose or as required by statutory retention periods under German law.
sections.dataRetentionText2: Business correspondence may be retained in accordance with applicable commercial and tax retention obligations.
sections.dataSecurityText: We implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data against accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure, or unauthorized access.
sections.dataSecurityText2: Data transmission between your browser and our website is encrypted using SSL or TLS technology.
sections.yourRightsIntro: You have the following rights under the GDPR:
yourRightsList: Right of access pursuant to Art. 15 GDPR
Right to rectification pursuant to Art. 16 GDPR
Right to erasure pursuant to Art. 17 GDPR
Right to restriction of processing pursuant to Art. 18 GDPR
Right to data portability pursuant to Art. 20 GDPR
Right to object pursuant to Art. 21 GDPR
Right to withdraw consent at any time pursuant to Art. 7(3) GDPR
sections.yourRightsNote: Where personal data is processed on the basis of Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, you have the right to object at any time on grounds relating to your particular situation.
sections.supervisoryAuthorityText: If you believe that the processing of your personal data violates applicable data protection law, you have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
sections.supervisoryAuthorityCompetent: The competent supervisory authority for Deepvac GmbH is:
sections.noAutomatedDecisionMakingText: We do not use automated decision-making, including profiling, within the meaning of Art. 22 GDPR in connection with this website.
sections.changesText: We reserve the right to update this Privacy Policy in order to reflect changes in legal requirements or changes to our website or our services. The version published on our website shall apply.

1.title: Parties and Contact
1.customerText: The contracting business customer as identified in the offer, Order, or order confirmation.

2.title: Definitions
2.c2: 2.2 "Customer" means the contracting party receiving Deliverables or Services from Deepvac.
2.c3: 2.3 "Affiliate" means any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party. Control means holding, directly or indirectly, more than 50 percent of the voting rights or otherwise having the ability to direct management and policies.
2.c4: 2.4 "Deliverables" means any hardware, parts, prototypes, assemblies, chamber systems, thermal subsystems, vacuum subsystems, control systems, PLC software, HMI software, firmware, models, drawings, documentation, test plans, acceptance criteria, test reports, data, and other work results provided by Deepvac.
2.c5: 2.5 "Services" means any testing services, engineering, design, development, consulting, integration, commissioning, training, maintenance, repair, retrofit, modernization, remote monitoring, data acquisition, and related activities performed by Deepvac.
2.c6: 2.6 "Order" means the Customer's purchase order, acceptance of an offer, or other instruction to proceed given in text form.
2.c7: 2.7 "Contract" means the binding agreement formed under clause 4, including all documents listed in clause 5.
2.c8: 2.8 "Software" means PLC programs, HMI applications, supervisory logic, control sequences, data acquisition routines, automation scripts, event logging configurations, interface drivers, and any other software developed or provided by Deepvac under the Contract.
2.c9: 2.9 "System" means a thermal vacuum chamber system, including all integrated mechanical, thermal, vacuum, electrical, instrumentation, and control components as specified in the Contract.
2.c10: 2.10 "Legacy System" means any existing equipment, infrastructure, controls, or installations at the Customer's site or in the Customer's possession that are not supplied by Deepvac under the respective Contract.
2.c11: 2.11 "FAT" means factory acceptance test performed at Deepvac's or its subcontractor's premises.
2.c12: 2.12 "SAT" means site acceptance test performed at the Customer's site after delivery, installation, or commissioning.
2.c13: 2.13 "Test Item" means any hardware, component, assembly, satellite, instrument, or other object provided by the Customer for testing by Deepvac.
2.c14: 2.14 "Working Day" means any day from Monday to Friday that is not a public holiday at Deepvac's registered seat (Lower Saxony, Germany). Where these Terms refer to days without further qualification, calendar days are meant.
2.c15: 2.15 "Text form" means text form within the meaning of Section 126b German Civil Code; email is sufficient unless mandatory law requires a stricter form.

3.title: Scope and Applicability
3.c1: 3.1 These General Terms and Conditions apply to all offers, Orders, deliveries, Services, and Contracts with Deepvac.
3.c2: 3.2 These Terms apply exclusively to entrepreneurs within the meaning of Section 14 German Civil Code, legal entities under public law, and special funds under public law. Contracts with consumers are excluded.
3.c3: 3.3 The Customer's terms and conditions do not apply, even if Deepvac does not object, unless Deepvac expressly agrees to them in text form.
3.c4: 3.4 Individual agreements in text form take precedence over these Terms.
3.c5: 3.5 These Terms also apply to all future offers, Orders, and Contracts with the Customer, even if they are not expressly referred to again. The version of these Terms published on Deepvac's website at the time of the Order applies, unless a different version is referenced in the offer or order confirmation.

4.title: Formation of Contract
4.c1: 4.1 Offers are non-binding unless expressly stated as binding in text form. Binding offers may be accepted within thirty calendar days from the offer date unless the offer states a different period.
4.c2: 4.2 A Contract is concluded when the Customer accepts a binding offer within the acceptance period, or otherwise only when Deepvac issues an order confirmation in text form or begins performance.
4.c3: 4.3 Oral agreements are not binding unless confirmed by Deepvac in text form.

5.title: Contract Documents and Order of Precedence
5.c1intro: 5.1 The Contract consists of, in descending order of precedence:
5.c1c: Statement of work, specification, test plan, acceptance criteria, and any agreed change orders
5.c1e: Any other documents expressly incorporated by reference in text form
5.c2: 5.2 Marketing statements, website content, brochures, and general technical descriptions are non-binding unless explicitly agreed as guaranteed characteristics in text form.

6.title: Scope of Performance
6.c1: 6.1 Deepvac shall provide Deliverables and Services only as expressly agreed in the Contract documents.
6.c2: 6.2 Deepvac may use qualified subcontractors. Deepvac remains responsible for its contractual obligations.
6.c3: 6.3 Unless expressly agreed, Deepvac does not owe third-party certifications, regulatory approvals, certification outcomes, country-specific approvals outside the European Union, or fitness for any specific purpose beyond the agreed specification. Deepvac's obligations as manufacturer regarding the conformity of the delivered System under clause 13.6 remain unaffected.
6.c4: 6.4 Deepvac may implement reasonable minor changes in design, components, or process if they do not materially impair the contractual purpose and are objectively reasonable for the Customer.

7.title: Change Requests
7.c1: 7.1 Any change to scope, parameters, schedule, acceptance criteria, interfaces, documentation, or Deliverables requires a change order in text form.
7.c2: 7.2 Deepvac will provide a change proposal including impact on price, schedule, and technical feasibility. Changes become binding only upon acceptance by both parties in text form.
7.c3: 7.3 If the Customer requests work before a change order is agreed, such work is performed on a time and materials basis and does not imply acceptance of a fixed price or deadline.

8.title: Customer Cooperation Duties
8.c1: 8.1 The Customer shall provide all information, decisions, access, samples, drawings, specifications, and materials required for performance in a timely manner and free of charge to Deepvac.
8.c2: 8.2 The Customer warrants that any items, materials, and instructions provided are safe, suitable, and compliant with applicable laws and regulations.
8.c3: 8.3 The Customer warrants that its data, materials, and instructions do not infringe third party rights. The Customer shall indemnify Deepvac against third party claims arising from such infringement, except to the extent caused by Deepvac.
8.c4: 8.4 If Customer cooperation is delayed or incomplete, Deepvac is entitled to extend deadlines and invoice additional effort and costs.

9.title: Prices, Taxes, and Payment
9.c1: 9.1 Prices are net prices plus applicable VAT and any other applicable taxes, duties, customs, or fees unless expressly included.
9.c2: 9.2 Unless otherwise agreed, invoices are payable within fourteen calendar days from the invoice date without deduction.
9.c3: 9.3 Unless otherwise agreed in text form, the following payment terms apply: for the supply of Systems and hardware under clauses 13 and 14, 70 percent of the order value upon order confirmation and 30 percent upon delivery; for Engineering Services, per agreed milestone or, absent milestones, monthly according to progress; for testing services, upon completion of the test campaign or per agreed test phase; for maintenance, repair, and other Services, after performance or monthly; for Service Agreements, in accordance with clause 17.9.
9.c4: 9.4 Deepvac may require advance payment, milestone payments, or security, especially for custom developments, prototypes, or high-value Orders.
9.c5: 9.5 The Customer may set off only claims that are undisputed, finally adjudicated, or ready for decision. Rights of retention apply only to claims arising from the same Contract. These restrictions do not apply to counterclaims of the Customer arising from defects of the Deliverables or Services under the same Contract.
9.c6: 9.6 In case of late payment, statutory default interest under German law applies. Deepvac may charge reasonable reminder and collection costs as permitted by law.
9.c7: 9.7 For Deliverables with an agreed delivery period of more than six months from Contract conclusion, the following applies: if Deepvac's procurement costs for materials, components, energy, or freight verifiably change by more than 5 percent in total between Contract conclusion and delivery, each party may request a corresponding adjustment of the affected prices, limited to the verified change in cost and its proportionate effect on the price. If a resulting price increase exceeds 10 percent of the agreed net order value, the Customer may terminate the affected Order with respect to the scope not yet delivered within fourteen calendar days of notification of the adjustment; Services already performed and costs already incurred shall be remunerated.
9.c8: 9.8 All prices are stated and payable in euros (EUR) unless expressly agreed otherwise in text form. Payments shall be made by bank transfer to the account stated in the invoice. The Customer bears all bank charges, intermediary bank fees, and currency conversion costs arising on its side, so that Deepvac receives the full invoiced amount. Withholding taxes or similar deductions required under the law of the Customer's country are borne by the Customer and the payment is grossed up accordingly, unless a double taxation treaty provides for relief and the Customer provides the required certificates in time.
9.c9: 9.9 For Customers whose registered seat is outside the European Union or the European Economic Area, Deepvac may make performance conditional on full advance payment, an irrevocable and confirmed letter of credit issued or confirmed by a bank acceptable to Deepvac, or another security acceptable to Deepvac. The costs of such security are borne by the Customer.
9.c10: 9.10 Deepvac issues invoices electronically, as a PDF document or as a structured electronic invoice, and sends them to the invoice address or email address designated by the Customer. The Customer shall designate such an address and keep it up to date.

10.title: Delivery, Deadlines, and Force Majeure
10.c1: 10.1 Dates and deadlines are non-binding unless expressly agreed as binding in text form.
10.c1a: 10.1a Contractual penalties, liquidated damages, or similar delay sanctions apply only if expressly agreed in text form in the respective order confirmation.
10.c2: 10.2 Delivery and performance periods start only after order confirmation, receipt of any agreed advance payment, and receipt of all Customer cooperation items required to start performance.
10.c3: 10.3 Force majeure includes events beyond Deepvac's reasonable control, including supply chain disruptions, transportation disruptions, governmental measures, export restrictions, sanctions, labor disputes, power failures, cyber incidents not caused by Deepvac, pandemics, and natural events, as well as incorrect or late delivery by suppliers for reasons not attributable to Deepvac, provided that Deepvac has concluded a congruent covering transaction. In such cases, obligations are suspended for the duration, and deadlines extend accordingly. If the event lasts longer than six months, either party may terminate the affected Order with respect to the scope not yet performed; Services already performed and costs already incurred shall be remunerated.
10.c4: 10.4 Deepvac may perform partial deliveries and partial Services if reasonable for the Customer.

11.title: Shipping, Risk Transfer, and Packaging
11.c1: 11.1 Unless otherwise agreed, delivery is FCA Deepvac's business address (Incoterms 2020). Risk transfers upon handover to the carrier nominated by the Customer or, where the Customer collects the goods itself, upon loading onto the collecting vehicle. Deepvac carries out export customs clearance. Where the parties agree on a different Incoterms 2020 rule in text form, the agreed rule governs delivery, transfer of risk, and the allocation of transport-related costs.
11.c2: 11.2 The Customer bears transport, insurance, customs, export, and import costs unless otherwise agreed.
11.c3: 11.3 Packaging is charged at cost unless otherwise agreed. Returnable packaging is accepted only by prior agreement in text form.
11.c4: 11.4 For deliveries to destinations outside the European Union, the Customer acts as importer of record and is responsible for import licenses, customs clearance in the country of destination, import duties and taxes, and compliance with local technical, safety, electrical, and regulatory requirements. Deepvac provides the conformity documentation applicable in the European Union. Country-specific certifications, markings, or approvals (for example UL, CSA, or local electrical standards) are owed only if expressly agreed in text form.
11.c5: 11.5 Where Deepvac performs Services at Customer sites outside Germany, the Customer shall support Deepvac in a timely manner in obtaining visas, work permits, site access, and local registrations required for Deepvac personnel and subcontractors. Delays caused by missing permits or access are treated as delays in Customer cooperation under clause 8.4.
11.c6: 11.6 If dispatch or collection is delayed at the Customer's request or for reasons within the Customer's responsibility, risk passes to the Customer upon notification of readiness for dispatch. Deepvac may charge storage costs of 0.5 percent of the net invoice value of the stored Deliverables per commenced month, unless the Customer proves that no or lower costs were incurred; the right to claim further damages remains unaffected.

12.title: Acceptance and Commissioning
12.c1: 12.1 If acceptance is agreed or legally required, acceptance criteria and procedure shall be defined in text form before the start of performance.
12.c2: 12.2 Where a factory acceptance test (FAT) is agreed, Deepvac shall notify the Customer when the Deliverables are ready for FAT. The Customer shall participate within the agreed timeframe or, absent an agreement, within fourteen calendar days of notification.
12.c3: 12.3 Where a site acceptance test (SAT) is agreed, the Customer shall ensure that the installation site, utilities, infrastructure, and all prerequisites specified in the Contract are ready and available before the agreed SAT date. Delays caused by incomplete site readiness shall be at the Customer's cost and risk.
12.c4: 12.4 Where commissioning is part of the scope, Deepvac shall perform commissioning according to the agreed procedure. Commissioning is complete once the tests agreed for this purpose have been successfully performed. Deepvac shall document completion in a commissioning protocol. The commissioning protocol does not replace acceptance unless expressly agreed in the Contract.
12.c5intro: 12.5 If no acceptance procedure is expressly agreed, acceptance occurs when Deepvac has notified the Customer in text form that the Deliverables are ready for acceptance and, in that notice, has informed the Customer of the acceptance mechanism under this clause and its consequences, and then:
12.c5a: the Customer confirms acceptance in text form, or
12.c5b: the Customer uses the Deliverables productively, or
12.c5c: a reasonable period of at least fourteen calendar days set in that notice expires without the Customer having refused acceptance within that period by identifying at least one defect in text form.
12.c6: 12.6 Minor defects that do not materially impair the contractual use do not prevent acceptance. Such defects shall be listed in the acceptance protocol and remedied by Deepvac within a reasonable period.
12.c7: 12.7 The Customer shall test and inspect Deliverables promptly within a reasonable period, taking into account the complexity of the Deliverables and the intended use.
12.c8: 12.8 Where the Contract provides for milestone-based or partial acceptance, each accepted milestone or partial delivery is deemed accepted independently. Subsequent milestones do not reopen acceptance of previously accepted deliverables.
12.c9: 12.9 If the Customer delays acceptance without identifying material defects, Deepvac may set a reasonable deadline in accordance with clause 12.5; upon expiry of that deadline, acceptance is deemed granted under the conditions of clause 12.5. Deepvac may invoice storage, standby, and additional costs incurred due to the delay.
12.c10: 12.10 Acceptance of Software and control system deliverables follows the same principles. Functionality is assessed against the agreed specification. Acceptance does not require the Software to be entirely free of minor anomalies that do not impair the agreed functionality.

13.title: Supply of Chamber Systems and Hardware
13.c1: 13.1 This clause applies to the supply of standardized and custom-engineered thermal vacuum chamber systems, chamber platforms, and related hardware.
13.c2: 13.2 The specification of the System is defined exclusively in the Contract documents. Dimensions, performance parameters, interfaces, and accessories are owed only as expressly agreed.
13.c3: 13.3 Standard chamber platforms are delivered in the configuration described in the applicable product documentation at the time of order confirmation. Options and upgrades are included only if expressly listed in the order confirmation.
13.c4: 13.4 Assembly, installation, and commissioning at the Customer's site are included only if expressly agreed. Where not included, Deepvac may offer these as separate Services.
13.c5: 13.5 The Customer is responsible for ensuring that the installation site meets the requirements specified by Deepvac, including but not limited to floor load capacity, room dimensions, access routes, power supply, cooling water, compressed air, and ventilation.
13.c6: 13.6 Where Deepvac supplies a complete System as a machine within the meaning of the applicable EU machinery legislation (Directive 2006/42/EC or, for products placed on the market from 20 January 2027, Regulation (EU) 2023/1230) for use within the European Union or the European Economic Area, Deepvac performs the conformity assessment for the System in the configuration delivered, affixes the CE marking, and provides the EU declaration of conformity together with the operating instructions and the technical documentation required by law. Where Deepvac supplies partly completed machinery or subsystems for integration by the Customer or a third party, Deepvac provides a declaration of incorporation and assembly instructions instead; the conformity assessment of the final machine is the responsibility of the party placing it on the market. Where Deepvac integrates Deliverables into a Legacy System, clauses 16.7 and 16.9 apply. Conformity under other EU legislation (for example the Low Voltage Directive, the EMC Directive, or the Pressure Equipment Directive) is covered to the extent such legislation applies to the delivered System. Any modification of the System by the Customer or a third party after delivery, including changes to safety functions, control software, or interlocks, is made at the Customer's own responsibility and may require a new conformity assessment by the Customer.
13.c7: 13.7 The Customer shall operate the System only in accordance with the operating instructions, within the specified operating limits, and with the safety functions, interlocks, and control software unchanged. Obligations relating to the workplace at the installation site, including the workplace risk assessment, the training of operating personnel, and periodic inspections required under occupational safety law, are the Customer's responsibility.

14.title: Custom Systems, Project Business, and Engineering Services
14.c1: 14.1 This clause applies to custom-engineered thermal vacuum systems, application-specific developments, and project-based engineering work.
14.c2: 14.2 The scope of the project is defined by the agreed specification, statement of work, and project plan. Performance beyond the agreed scope requires a change order under clause 7.
14.c3: 14.3 Engineering decisions within the agreed specification are at Deepvac's professional discretion unless the Contract requires Customer approval for specific decisions.
14.c4: 14.4 The Customer shall designate a competent project contact and shall make timely decisions on open points. Delayed decisions entitle Deepvac to adjust the schedule and invoice additional costs.
14.c5: 14.5 Where the project involves integration with the Customer's existing infrastructure, the Customer is responsible for providing accurate and complete documentation of the existing systems, interfaces, and site conditions.
14.c6: 14.6 Deepvac may propose reasonable design alternatives if the originally agreed solution proves technically impracticable or disproportionately costly. Such alternatives require agreement under the change order procedure.
14.c7: 14.7 Where the Order covers engineering, design, or consulting services only (for example concepts, feasibility studies, calculations, drawings, specifications, parts lists, control concepts, or design packages) without the supply or manufacture of hardware by Deepvac ("Engineering Services"), clauses 14.8 to 14.11 apply in addition.
14.c8: 14.8 The Deliverables of Engineering Services are the documents and data expressly listed in the Order, in the agreed format and level of detail. Unless expressly agreed, Deepvac does not owe manufacturing-ready production documentation, procurement, supplier management, manufacturing supervision, installation, commissioning, or acceptance of the resulting system.
14.c9: 14.9 If the Customer or a third party procures components or manufactures, assembles, installs, or operates a system on the basis of Deepvac's Engineering Services, the Customer is solely responsible for the selection and quality of the procured components, for the correct implementation of the design, for the conformity assessment and CE marking of the resulting machine or system, and for its safe operation. Deepvac's liability is governed by clauses 20 and 21 and is limited to damage attributable to a defect in Deepvac's own Deliverables.
14.c10: 14.10 Where agreed, Engineering Services are performed in milestones or work packages. Each milestone is reviewed in a milestone meeting; acceptance is governed by clause 12. Comments by the Customer on a milestone that go beyond the agreed specification are change requests under clause 7.
14.c11: 14.11 Unless expressly agreed otherwise in text form, the Customer receives, upon full payment, a non-exclusive, perpetual right to use the Deliverables of Engineering Services for the manufacture, operation, maintenance, and modification of the specific system described in the Order, including by third parties acting on the Customer's behalf. Clause 22 applies in all other respects; in particular, Deepvac's pre-existing know-how, calculation methods, and templates remain with Deepvac and are not transferred. Native CAD and source files are delivered only if expressly agreed; otherwise Deliverables are provided in neutral exchange formats (for example PDF, STEP).

15.title: Testing Services
15.c1: 15.1 This clause applies to thermal vacuum testing, environmental simulation, test campaign execution, and related testing services.
15.c2: 15.2 Testing shall be performed according to the agreed test plan. If no test plan is agreed, testing shall be performed according to Deepvac's standard procedures appropriate to the assignment.
15.c3: 15.3 The Customer remains solely responsible for the design, intended use, safety, legal conformity, and regulatory compliance of the Test Item.
15.c4: 15.4 Test results are valid only for the tested configuration and boundary conditions documented in the test report. Any extrapolation to other configurations, environments, or use cases is at the Customer's risk.
15.c5: 15.5 Deepvac does not guarantee certification outcomes, regulatory approvals, mission success, or fitness for purpose beyond the agreed test specification.
